parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national passport sex-marker restrictions and entry-refusal cable (with lifetime-ineligibility risk for alleged misrepresentation) meet a division that bars trans people from facilities by birth sex, bars trans women from women's shelters, places inmates by birth sex, and closes document changes. A 2019 indecent-exposure definition and an enforceable 2023 ban on gender-expressive performance add criminal presentation exposure, though no trans-specific enforcement is documented. Minor-care bans reach families through regret suits. No divisional protections operate for trans people. Violence data rests on an undercount floor and is treated as undocumented. Universal-exposure measures with no working remedy place this well below the 0.25 tier and in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports show birth sex; 'X' markers stopped for new issue; entry cable directs refusal on any document discrepancy and raises lifetime-ineligibility review for alleged misrepresentation. Detentions of citizens abroad and stranded travellers are documented.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; federal civil-liberties litigation unresolved; no documented operative protection for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Divisional closure of document change (2023 sex-by-anatomy law, 1977 birth-certificate bar) means no local document route; national refusal at entry is the operative control.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Birth-sex placement of trans inmates by division statute; national immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections adopted conversion-style policies. Bathroom trespass arrest documented (24h hold in men's ward).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for custody; the prison-axis source is a single encyclopedia article with no operative remedy shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can move into detention, then birth-sex placement by the state or national custody; the state and federal layers reinforce each other.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Universal birth-sex facility rules: 2026 act requires birth-sex use of facilities, bars trans women from shelters; 2019 law treats bathroom use matching identity as indecent exposure; national funding and facility orders apply. Bathroom trespass statute enforced once.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No divisional facilities protection; the 2021 school-bathroom ban remains in litigation and no protective operating regime is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facility rules govern public buildings and shelters; the 2019 indecent-exposure definition raises the stakes of any identity-matching use, and national measures compound this for federal sites.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care banned for minors (upheld June 2025) and for inmates (April 2024); regret suits and $25,000 provider actions; adults who help minors face civil penalties; national proposals would cut public reimbursement for under-18s.
care_services.protection: Not documented for trans adults' care access in the division.
care_services.interaction: Care denial at a clinic can expose a visitor's medical history to officials; for travellers with minors, care is criminally and civilly exposed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Enforceable 2023 ban on 'male or female impersonators' in places a child could see; Class A/E penalties upheld on appeal. Government employees may refuse marriages. Police and officials reported turning a blind eye to assaults (reporting from April 2021); 2024 index ranks state among lowest for LGBTQ rights.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The 2021 small-business sign mandate is struck and not in force; the drag-ban suit is ongoing without status.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Presentation law and facility laws together give police a basis to act against a visibly gender-nonconforming visitor, with no documented trans-specific enforcement recorded.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor-care ban with regret suits against parents, guardians and physicians; school-outing rule requires reporting of name or pronoun requests to parents; national school prosecution directive; birth-sex sports rules; foster and adoption religious-refusal law.
minors_guardians.protection: Teacher shield for birth-certificate pronouns is protective only for teachers, not travellers; no minor-specific protection documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's care or school exposure can make a guardian a subject of investigation or suit; a family traveller carries the consequences of the care ban.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Killings of trans women at 7.8 per 100k reported, but the dossier labels this an undercount floor on 10 deaths; per the rubric this is no usable evidence. Gay and trans panic defence remains available. Recorded anti-trans incidents 0, 1, 2 (2019–2021) are raw, without denominators.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime statute omits gender identity; a 2019 chief prosecutor opinion supports gender-based enhancement, a partial mitigation with no documented case shown.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police non-response and the panic defence make reporting less protective, but the violence axis stays undocumented for magnitude.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Divisional remedies are narrow: no statewide non-discrimination law; municipal ordinances preempted for private employers; religious-refusal adoption and marriage laws. Pending suits on the 2026 act, facilities, prison care ban and licence marker are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment law (2018/2020 rulings) and national hate-crimes statute apply; marriage recognised nationally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: National protections do not reach the state's public-accommodation or document gaps; unresolved litigation means present enforcement cannot be predicted.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest analogue: birth-sex prison housing and a cross-dressing crime in administrative buildings. This case adds birth-sex shelters, facility rules for public and shelter settings, a closed document regime, a performance-presentation felony and minor-care exposure, so it sits lower. Both lack capital exposure, so it stays above the lethal-custody tier.

The 0.15 tier documents arrests for presentation, custody assaults with blocked witnesses and capital provisions. Here, custody harm is documented only nationally and there is no capital pathway or recorded visitor custody violence, so this is clearly higher.

Registration and database exposure is universal, as here through birth-sex document checks. The 0.45 case has no birth-sex facility bans, no custody placement rule and no criminal presentation ban, so this case is lower.

parsed.synthesis: Universal-exposure measures dominate: the document regime, national entry-refusal guidance, birth-sex facility and shelter rules, and birth-sex custody placement all apply to every visitor who is outed or outable, with no working remedy shown. A criminal presentation ban and a bathroom-related indecent-exposure definition add enforceable legal exposure, and minor-care bans and school-outing rules carry risk for travelling families. Recourse is limited to national employment and hate-crime law and pending litigation; divisional protections are narrow and preempted. Violence data is an undercount floor and so is not weighed; absence of documented visitor cases is not treated as safety. Overall the combined regime places this case in High Risk.
